extracted.intended_audience: readers of philosophical/personal essays; people interested in simple living, self-reliance, and practical homesteading
extracted.subtask_short: writing personal essay on simple living
extracted.subtask_description: A first‑person, reflective nonfiction essay advocating simple, self-reliant living and practical economy; combines philosophical aphorism with concrete, practical detail (e.g., building, budgeting, gardening).

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfy more pressing wants first
rubrics_metrics.description: Their principle were to satisfy the more pressing wants first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize essential needs (shelter, food, warmth) before aesthetic or luxury additions. Example/anti-pattern: early colonists built cellar-houses to be dry and fed rather than expending time/money on superstructures; rushing to ornamentation before necessities is imprudent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Line houses with beauty where they meet life, not overlay
rubrics_metrics.description: Let our houses first be lined with beauty, where they come in contact with our lives, like the tenement of the shellfish, and not overlaid with it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply beauty/function where it actually affects lived experience (interiors, functional surfaces) rather than superficial exterior ornamentation. Anti-pattern: houses heavily ornamented externally but lacking inward suitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept technological advantages but use materials wisely
rubrics_metrics.description: Though we might live in a cave... it certainly is better to accept the advantages, though so dearly bought, which the invention and industry of mankind offer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use available manufactured materials (boards, shingles, lime) thoughtfully to improve life without becoming enslaved to luxury. With ingenuity, common materials can produce greater wealth and make civilization a blessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value building with one's own hands
rubrics_metrics.description: There is some of the same fitness in a man’s building his own house that there is in a bird’s building its own nest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage in construction and manual work yourself when possible—it develops poetic faculty and authentic engagement with life. Anti-pattern: delegating all construction to contractors so one 'plays' life rather than lives it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid excessive division of labor; don't outsource thinking
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not desirable that he should do so to the exclusion of my thinking for myself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain personal involvement in a variety of tasks (mental and manual). Beware a social system where roles are so specialized that individuals cease to practice full human capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let architectural beauty grow from the indweller's necessities and character
rubrics_metrics.description: What of architectural beauty I now see, I know has gradually grown from within outward, out of the necessities and character of the indweller...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and ornamentation should emerge organically from inhabitants' needs and character rather than imposed fashions. Anti-pattern: sentimental reformers who start at the cornice (superficial decoration) rather than the foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer unpretending dwellings that reflect life
rubrics_metrics.description: The most interesting dwellings... are the most unpretending, humble log huts and cottages of the poor commonly; it is the life of the inhabitants whose shells they are...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A dwelling's interest and aesthetic come from the life within; modest structures honestly lived in are preferable to ostentatious shells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Build deliberately — foundation before ornament
rubrics_metrics.description: It would be worth the while to build still more deliberately... perchance never raising any superstructure until we found a better reason for it than our temporal necessities even.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider functional foundations for doors, windows, cellars, garrets prior to adding superstructure or ornament. Anti-pattern: hasty building that emphasizes appearance over practical foundation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism toward vanity monuments and wasteful spending on stone
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations are possessed with an insane ambition to perpetuate the memory of themselves by the amount of hammered stone they leave... What if equal pains were taken to smooth and polish their manners?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer investments in moral and intellectual culture over grand monuments. Critique of public expenditure for vanity architecture.

rubrics_metrics.name: Students (and learners) should combine manual and intellectual work
rubrics_metrics.description: The student who secures his coveted leisure and retirement by systematically shirking any labor necessary to man obtains but an ignoble and unprofitable leisure... they should not play life, or study it merely, while the community supports them at this expensive game, but earnestly live it from beginning to end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational formation should include practical, hands-on experience (building, farming) alongside intellectual study. Example: laying foundations themselves rather than only attending lectures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be wary of inventions that are means to unimproved ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Our inventions are wont to be pretty toys, which distract our attention from serious things. They are but improved means to an unimproved end...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge new technologies by whether they improve substantive ends, not merely speed or connectivity. Anti-pattern: building a telegraph or railroad without regard to the value of what is communicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not postpone life for the pursuit of money
rubrics_metrics.description: This spending of the best part of one’s life earning money in order to enjoy a questionable liberty during the least valuable part of it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer living fully in the present (e.g., travel on foot, simplicity) rather than sacrificing youth/health to accumulate means for a doubtful later enjoyment. Example: walking thirty miles saves fare and offers fuller experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate only what suffices for your needs; spade rather than plough when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If one would live simply and eat only the crop which he raised... he would need to cultivate only a few rods of ground, and that it would be cheaper to spade up that than to use oxen to plough it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match scale and methods of cultivation to actual needs; small-scale, hand-worked plots can be more economical and freer than large animal-powered agriculture tied to markets and obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dependence on animals or tools that make you their servant
rubrics_metrics.description: I should never have broken a horse or bull and taken him to board for any work he might do for me, for fear I should become a horse-man or a herds-man merely...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of adopting labor-saving devices that require upkeep or ownership burdens which in turn constrain your freedom; consider trade-offs between convenience and independence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and openly report material costs and economies
rubrics_metrics.description: I give the details because very few are able to tell exactly what their houses cost... These are all the materials excepting the timber stones and sand, which I claimed by squatter’s right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document expenses and yields (itemized costs of building, food, farm outgoes and returns) to make claims about economy verifiable. Example: Thoreau's itemized house cost and farm income showing shelter cheaper than rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment practically and learn from experience rather than deference to authority
rubrics_metrics.description: I learned from the experience of both years, not being in the least awed by many celebrated works on husbandry... that if one would live simply... he would need to cultivate only a few rods...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct hands-on experiments and adjust practice based on results rather than blind adherence to celebrated authorities or theories. Anti-pattern: deferring to celebrated treatises (e.g., Arthur Young) without practical trial.
